cells.tense: You are at the edge of leaving something that mattered, with the pen in your hand.
cells.act: put the problem down and take a walk with nothing to solve
cells.ask: Put the problem down for the walk. Ten minutes, nothing to solve. If a name comes up, let it come up and keep walking.
cells.core:
You're at the edge of something you were part of, and you know better than most what it gave you. The pull is toward what connects deeper, and you're moving that way without a verdict on what you're leaving. The head has already worked through why, and now it wants to work it through again — that is what a mind at rest does when it is left alone.

Put the problem down for the walk. Ten minutes, nothing to solve. If a name comes up, let it come up and keep walking. The part of this that can be settled by thinking it through is mostly settled. What's left doesn't want another pass; it wants you to stop carrying it while you walk. You don't have to decide anything on the way.
cells.sheetLine: You're walking on from something, and the thinking is done.
cells.verb: Walking on from what has been gathered, toward what connects deeper
cells.place: Where what has been must fully end for what comes next

cells.tense: You are bracing for the leaving and building the next thing before the old one has finished.
cells.act: build the first new thing from what the clearing showed
cells.ask: Build the first small thing from what the leaving already showed you. One thing, not the whole next chapter. Build it where the old one stood.
cells.core:
You're bracing for the leaving and building the next thing before the old one has finished. A talk about what's ending gets a plan attached, and the plan gets a backup plan, because a threshold that isn't managed looks like a fall. The leaving is real; the scaffolding stacked around it is not the leaving.

Build the first small thing from what the leaving already showed you. One thing, not the whole next chapter. Build it where the old one stood, and stop there. The weight you're carrying is a plan for a road that hasn't been laid yet. One honest thing, started now, is the size the moment can hold; the rest shows itself once something is standing.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a threshold that has already been crossed.
cells.act: cut through the story to what actually follows
cells.ask: Take one story you've told about why it ended, and write what actually follows from it. One line. Follow that line, not the story.
cells.core:
You're standing at a threshold that has already been crossed. The meaning of it keeps getting re-read, the way a letter gets re-read when the hand won't put it down. Somewhere in there is a version of why it ended that no longer matches what you know, and you keep returning to the old edge to test it.

Take one story you've told about why it ended, and write what actually follows from it. One line. Follow that line, not the story. The thinking part is already strong; it just keeps being spent on the same closed account. Aim it one step forward and it does what it's good at: it shows you what follows, and what follows is not there.
cells.sheetLine: You're standing at a threshold you've already crossed.

cells.place: Where what has been must fully end for what comes next

cells.tense: You are walking on from what you gathered without seeing your own part in the leaving.
cells.act: let the mind rest instead of working the problem
cells.ask: Sit still for a few minutes and stop working the leaving. Not to decide anything. Just let it rest, and notice it was your call to walk.
cells.core:
You've been walking on from what you gathered, and your version has it that the leaving happened to you. In the telling, the threshold arrived and you crossed it, which is true, and the crossings were your steps. Other people's versions get the credit for what you saw earlier than they did. You keep arriving where the meaning moves next without marking that you moved first.

Sit still for a few minutes and stop working the leaving. Not to decide anything. Just let it rest, and notice it was your call to walk. You don't have to make a speech of it to anyone. The walking toward what connects deeper was something you did — you can know that quietly, and the threshold settles.
cells.sheetLine: You walked on first, and you'd say it happened to you.

attempts.check: The record says the passage threshold is drawing-level; at Balanced the growth invitation is Repose, whose acts are all rest-acts, so the reading is that rest settles a crossing already underway — a reader whose crossing has stalled might say rest is the wrong medicine. The ask survives being wrong: sitting still for ten minutes and leaving the problem alone costs nothing and teaches how much of the crossing is being solved in the head. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is 'You can be part of something without carrying it,' which decides in advance what the leaving means when the record only says a threshold has been reached.

attempts.check: The refused cells slid because the ask's 'build' invited me to inflate the Too Much reading into a universal about conversation and to certify what is already known. Rewritten: one conversation-shaped sentence, no claim about what is known, no refrains, and the Too Little door-phrase replaced with a different image entirely. The unsupported claim that remains is only that a crossed threshold is being re-walked — a reader could say they simply haven't fully left, which the ask survives: writing one line about what follows costs nothing either way. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person was status 2's second half; it is now sized to the act instead of to the life.
